author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Set up EmuCoreX safely on the first run
summary: A clean first-run path for Android: choose the safe profile, identify the GPU family, connect a personal BIOS dump, grant durable folder access, and confirm one game before changing advanced settings.
heroAlt: A first-run setup wizard illustrating the configuration stage before an emulator library is opened

blocks.text: Prepare three things before launching EmuCoreX: a BIOS image dumped from a PlayStation 2 that you own, one or more folders containing personal disc images, and a destination folder for emulator data. Keep the BIOS and game folders separate. The emulator-data folder will hold memory cards, save states, patches, texture packs and logs, so choose a location that Android will keep accessible rather than a temporary download or messaging-app folder.

Safe baseline: use the Optimal / Safe startup profile, leave advanced speed hacks at their defaults, and test one known-good game before changing graphics or CPU options. A faster-looking preset is not useful if it hides the cause of a crash or rendering fault.

items: 1. Read the introduction, continue to the startup-profile page, and select Optimal / Safe.
2. On the GPU page, use Show detected processor. Confirm the reported SoC, then select the closest chipset and GPU branch instead of guessing from the phone brand.
3. Choose BIOS File and select the main BIOS image from your own dump. A normal dump is commonly a .bin or .rom file; do not select a compressed archive or a downloaded firmware pack.
4. Add one game folder through Android's folder picker. Grant access to the folder itself, not to an individual game file, so the permission remains useful after a library refresh.
5. Choose the emulator-data folder. The default is appropriate for most phones; a custom folder is useful when you deliberately manage backups or move data between devices.
6. Continue only when the BIOS and game-folder rows both report Ready, then wait for Preparing your library to finish.

blocks.text: Android's document picker can show cloud providers, SD cards and app-specific locations side by side. Prefer local internal storage for the first test. If an SD card is used, select its game folder through the picker so EmuCoreX receives a persistent Storage Access Framework permission; typing or copying a filesystem path is not equivalent. Avoid moving or renaming the selected folder until the library has been verified.

items: The Home screen reports a ready BIOS and at least one library folder.
A manual library refresh completes without a missing-folder warning.
One personally dumped game opens its detail page and starts with the default renderer.
An in-game save written to a PS2 memory card is still visible after closing and reopening the app.
The emulator-data folder contains the expected subfolders and remains available after an Android reboot.

blocks.text: Run the first test for several minutes without enabling frame skipping, changing cycle rates or installing a custom GPU driver. Watch for stable audio, correct aspect ratio and a consistent frame rate. The objective is not maximum resolution; it is a reproducible reference point. Record the renderer and internal-resolution values that worked so later experiments can be compared against a known configuration.

If the first game fails, return to Settings and restore the Optimal / Safe performance profile before changing anything else. Re-select the BIOS file if its row says Files not found, and re-authorize a game folder if Android revoked access. If a custom emulator-data folder was moved, point EmuCoreX to its new location rather than creating a second empty folder with the same name. Reset only the per-game profile when one title is affected; preserve global settings when the rest of the library still works.

items: BIOS rejected: the selected file is an archive, a partial component, unreadable, or not a clean personal dump.
Empty library: access was granted to the wrong level of the folder tree, the image format is unsupported, or the folder permission was lost.
Black screen on one title: test a full boot and the default renderer before applying game-specific fixes.
Immediate slowdown: return internal resolution to native and check sustained device temperature before using speed hacks.
Settings seem duplicated: confirm that only one emulator-data folder is active and back up the older folder before removing anything.

blocks.text: Once this baseline passes, make one change at a time and retest the same scene. Renderer choice, internal resolution, driver selection and game-specific fixes are independent variables; changing all of them together makes a regression impossible to diagnose. Keep in-game memory-card saves as the durable record and treat save states as temporary checkpoints. That discipline turns the initial setup into a stable foundation instead of a collection of unexplained tweaks.
